issues.failure_explanation: For fixed R, as h→0 the upper bound \overline{\lambda}_k = \lambda_{k,h}^{R,\mathrm{P1}} tends to \lambda_k^R > \lambda_k, and the lower bound \underline{\lambda}_k tends to \mu_k^{R,N}(V)(1-\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R)) \le \lambda_k, which is strictly below \lambda_k whenever \mu_k^{R,N} < \lambda_k/(1-\lambda_k^R/\sigma(R)) — generically true; e.g. at R=4 for V_1 the limit is \approx 1.75\times0.992 \approx 1.736 < \lambda_1 \approx 1.74. Only the joint limit h_{\max}\to0 together with R\to\infty (using \mu_k^{R,N}\to\lambda_k and \sigma(R)\to\infty) yields convergence to the true eigenvalue.

failure_location.quote: As $h_{\max}\to0$, $\overline{V}\to V$ and $\lambda_{k,h}^{R,\mathrm{P1}}\to\lambda_k^R$, so the bounds converge to the true eigenvalues.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing limit: 'As h_{\max}\to0 and R\to\infty, the bounds converge to the true eigenvalues' — a one-line quantifier repair with no loss of content.
issues.overall_effect: Only the asymptotic-consistency sentence after eq:bounds is affected; the rigorous two-sided bounds for fixed (R,h) in eq:bounds, the tables, and all formal results remain valid.
issues.title: Convergence claim omits the R→∞ limit; fixed-R bounds do not converge to λ_k as h→0
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single added limit in a prose sentence; the method, the rigorous fixed-R guarantees, the rates, and the advertised scope all survive unchanged, so no mathematical content is lost.

All exceed the claimed 0.01%; the claim holds only for V_1, k=1 (\approx 0.005%). The same false figure is repeated in the Conclusion.
